column11:
The biographies of Lady Grisell Baillie, Lady Fanshawe, the Countess of Balcarres, Elizabeth Smith and Madame Swetchine are “By the author of ‘The Heir of Redclyffe’”. 

Olympia Morata and Amalie Sieveking are signed E.T. and the work of Emily Taylor. So, according to CMY, is the unsigned article on Mum Bet (perhaps unsigned because derivative of the work of Harriet Martineau). Anna Gurney is signed by Sarah Austin. Princess Galitzin is signed H. D.. Mrs Hutchinson, Caroline Perthes and Lady Russell are attributed to \'the author of Magdalen Stafford\', who may have been Mrs Bromfield.   Elizabeth Carter and Anne Grant of Laggan are unsigned and the work of Ann Carter Smith.  Elizabeth Fry is unsigned.

 A second series of biographies was published in 1865.

column2: \'Biographies of Eminent Anglicans\'
column8: NA
column11: CMY contributed to a series of short biographies of Anglican saints at the behest of the Rev. [[person:221]J. F. W. Bullock], Rector of Radwinter. In 1902 he finally published the first three volumes of a projected six volume work called Daily Lections for every Morning and Evening throughout the Year (London: Rivington 1902). Volume V of this work, described in his preface, was to have consisted of \'Lections on Anglican Worthies, arranged as additional Readings for Sunday\'. These \'Biographies of Eminent Anglicans\' exist in MS and are catalogued under that name among the Bullock papers in the Bodleian Library, Oxford, but were never published, since no more of the Daily Lections ever appeared.
